items.title: Gerald Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I played it with Gloster Current’s band.

ctx.x: Then it wasn’t until three years later that they let a black make a record. Kid Ory they let make a couple of sides, a couple of sides. But as I say, King Oliver and Jelly Roll made a number together, King Porter Stomp, which by the way the reason it’s named, and King Porter Stomp was the biggest jazz number. If your band didn’t have an arrangement of King Porter Stomp, you were not in. King Porter Stomp is one hell of a composition. It’s, I plan to write it one day. If you hear, if you hear what’s-his-name…
We only have a few minutes left.
